mainTopic: Overlapping ארבע אמות zones, and whether חפצי הפקר acquire שביתה according to רבי יוחנן בן נורי (the rain and cistern proofs)
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about people limited to ארבע אמות whose zones overlap. The משנה then gives a rule for three people in a row, and רבי שמעון compares that case to three courtyards joined by עירובין. The גמרא opens with רבא asking why רבי יוחנן בן נורי gives a sleeping traveler 2000 אמות. Is it because חפצי הפקר acquire שביתה, or only because a sleeper is treated like someone awake? רב יוסף proves the first option from a ברייתא about rain that fell before יום טוב. רב ספרא challenges that proof. אביי answers with a contradiction between a משנה and a ברייתא about public cisterns, and רב יוסף gives a simpler answer from the wording of the rain ברייתא itself. The גמרא then asks why rain that falls on יום טוב did not acquire שביתה in the ocean or in the clouds. It answers with clouds formed before יום טוב, and with the rule that water absorbed in a cloud cannot acquire שביתה. Because of that second answer, the attempt to prove that there are no תחומין above ten טפחים fails.

steps.title: The condition for two people sharing their overlapping area
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its rule about two people whose ארבע אמות overlap. They may eat together in the shared middle area, but neither may carry from his own private zone into the other's private zone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Provided that this one does not carry anything from inside his own area into the area of his fellow.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a limit to the rule on the previous amud. Two people with overlapping ארבע אמות may bring food into the shared overlap and eat there, but only under one condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each person may move objects only within his own ארבע אמות. The overlap belongs to both of them, so both may use it. The part of the zone that belongs only to one person is off-limits to the other. So carrying from 'mine only' into 'yours only' is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Provided that (introduces a condition)
Four cubits, the limited zone of someone who has no full תחום
He may not carry out (move an object outside its allowed area)
His fellow, the other person

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about carrying between private and public domains (הוצאה in the usual sense). It is about people who, because of תחומין rules, may move objects only within ארבע אמות of where they are.

phrases.english: provided that this one does not carry out
phrases.notes: Continuation of the two-person case begun on the previous amud

phrases.english: from within his own area into that of his fellow.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יוֹצִיא זֶה מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה's two-person ruling earlier
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two people with overlapping ארבע אמות may use the shared area, but neither may carry from his exclusive zone into the other's.

steps.title: Three people in a row with the middle one overlapping both
steps.stepSummary: If three people stand in a row, the middle person's zone overlaps with each of the outer two. The middle person may eat with either one, and each may eat with him. The two outer people may not eat with each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there were three, and the middle one's area overlapped with each of the others: he is permitted with them, and they are permitted with him. But the two outer ones are forbidden with each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה expands the case from two people to three in a row. It tells us who may share space with whom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sharing is allowed only where two zones actually overlap. The middle person overlaps with both neighbors, so he can share with each of them. The outer two have no common area at all, so they are forbidden to share with each other, even though each one is connected to the middle person.

keyTerms.meaning: The middle one
Absorbed or overlapping into another's area
The outer ones
Permitted / forbidden

steps.whyThisMatters: The principle is that permission does not 'pass through' a middle party. Two people must share an actual common area. This idea returns in the courtyard comparison in the next step.

phrases.english: if there were three
and the middle one is overlapped between them —
he is permitted with them,
and they are permitted with him,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁנַיִם הַחִיצוֹנִים אֲסוּרִין זֶה עִם זֶה.
phrases.english: but the two outer ones are forbidden with each other.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיוּ שְׁלֹשָׁה וְהָאֶמְצָעִי מוּבְלָע בֵּינֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the two-person rule to a three-person case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The middle person may share with each outer person, but the two outer people may not share with each other.

steps.title: רבי שמעון compares the case to three courtyards
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון explains the three-person ruling with a parallel case. Three courtyards open into each other and into the public domain. The two outer courtyards each made an עירוב with the middle one, but not with each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: What is this like? It is like three courtyards that open into one another and also open into the public domain. If the two outer ones made an עירוב with the middle one, the middle one is permitted with them and they are permitted with it. But the two outer ones are forbidden with each other.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives a familiar example from עירובי חצירות to show that the three-person ruling makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each outer courtyard is joined to the middle courtyard by its own עירוב. Nothing joins the two outer courtyards to each other, so they stay forbidden to each other. This matches the three people exactly: a link to the middle does not create a link between the two ends.

keyTerms.meaning: To what is this comparable? (introduces an analogy)
Courtyards
The public domain
They made an עירוב (joined their areas for carrying)

steps.whatToRemember: In both the people case and the courtyard case, A–B and B–C connections do not create an A–C connection. Only a direct link or a shared area allows sharing.
steps.confusionAlert: Each courtyard also opens to the public domain. This tells us the outer courtyards are not forced to pass through the middle one. Each has its own exit, so each must make its own עירוב to be joined to the middle courtyard.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said:
to what is the matter comparable —
to three courtyards that open into one another,
and open into the public domain.
if the two made an eiruv with the middle one —
it is permitted with them
and they are permitted with it,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁתַּיִם הַחִיצוֹנוֹת אֲסוּרוֹת זוֹ עִם זוֹ.
phrases.english: but the two outer ones are forbidden with each other.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an analogy that supports and explains the three-person ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Courtyards joined to a middle courtyard by separate עירובין may each carry with the middle one but not with each other.

steps.title: רבא asks what רבי יוחנן בן נורי's reasoning is
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with רבא asking about the reasoning of רבי יוחנן בן נורי. Earlier in the משנה, רבי יוחנן בן נורי ruled that a person who slept on the road when שבת began still gets 2000 אמות. רבא suggests one possible reason: חפצי הפקר acquire שביתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבא asked: What does רבי יוחנן בן נורי hold? Does he hold that ownerless objects acquire a שבת residence?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to an earlier ruling in the משנה and asks why רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds it. This step gives only the first side of the question. Steps 5-6 complete it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן נורי gives a sleeping traveler a full תחום even though he could not have intended to set his residence. רבא's first suggestion is that רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds a broad rule: even an ownerless object, which has no person's intent behind it, automatically acquires שביתה. If that is true, a sleeping person, who also has no active intent, acquires שביתה too.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (introduces a question or dilemma)
What does he hold? (asks for the reasoning behind a ruling)
Ownerless objects
Acquire a שבת residence (the spot from which their 2000 אמות are measured)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן בן נורי does not appear in the משנה text on this amud. He is quoted from the earlier משנה about someone who fell asleep on the road. Also, do not treat 'ownerless objects acquire שביתה' as the conclusion. It is only the first option רבא raises, and the second option comes in Step 6.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rava asked:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי קָסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי?
phrases.english: What does Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri hold?
Does he hold
that ownerless objects acquire residence?
phrases.notes: First side of the dilemma. The alternative continues next.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רָבָא מַאי קָסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא by returning to an earlier ruling in the משנה, not to the courtyard analogy just before it
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying reasoning of רבי יוחנן בן נורי's ruling that a sleeping traveler acquires שביתה. Specifically, whether it comes from a general principle that ownerless objects acquire שביתה.

steps.title: First side: he should argue about utensils too, but a person shows the רבנן's strength
steps.stepSummary: רבא continues the first side of his question. If רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds that חפצי הפקר acquire שביתה, he should also argue about ownerless כלים. The dispute is set about a person to show that the רבנן reject even the strong argument 'awake acquires, so asleep acquires.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And by right he should have argued about utensils too. The reason they argue about a person is to show you how strong the רבנן's position is. Even though one could say, 'Since an awake person acquires, a sleeping one also acquires,' the משנה teaches us that he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is still building the first possible reason for רבי יוחנן בן נורי. He is answering an obvious problem with that reason: why does the משנה only mention a person?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ownerless things acquire שביתה on their own, then ownerless utensils should also get 2000 אמות. That would make כלים a natural place for the dispute. רבא explains that a sleeping person was chosen on purpose. He is the hardest case for the רבנן, and they still say he does not acquire.

keyTerms.meaning: By right / logically it should be
Utensils, objects
To show you how far the רבנן go in their position

keyTerms.term: הוֹאִיל וְנֵיעוֹר קָנָה, יָשֵׁן נָמֵי קָנָה
keyTerms.meaning: Since one who is awake acquires, one who is asleep also acquires
It teaches us (the new point being taught)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two arguments. Here, the 'awake/asleep' argument is the reasoning the רבנן REJECT. It is not רבי יוחנן בן נורי's main reason in this first side. His reason here is that ownerless things acquire שביתה.

phrases.english: And by right he should have argued about utensils too.
phrases.notes: If ownerless objects acquire residence, ownerless utensils would also get 2000 אמות.

phrases.english: And the reason they argue about a person
is to let you know the strength of the Rabbis' view,
that even though one could argue:
since an awake person acquires,
a sleeping person also acquires,
it teaches us that he does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְדִין הוּא דְּלִיפְלוֹג בְּכֵלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the first side of רבא's question by handling the problem of why the dispute is about a person and not utensils.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יוחנן בן נורי's reason is that ownerless objects acquire שביתה. If so, the choice of a person is explained as showing the רבנן's strength.

steps.title: Second side: ownerless things don't acquire, but a sleeper is like an awake person
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives the other possibility. Maybe רבי יוחנן בן נורי generally holds that חפצי הפקר do NOT acquire שביתה. He gives the sleeper 2000 אמות only because one who would acquire while awake also acquires while asleep.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds that, in general, ownerless objects do not acquire residence. Here the reason is: since an awake person acquires, a sleeping one also acquires.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא presents the second half of his question. This is a different reason that would also explain רבי יוחנן בן נורי's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this approach, ownerless utensils would NOT get their own 2000 אמות. The sleeper's ruling rests only on a special logic for people. A person who sleeps is treated as if he were awake and had chosen this spot. Both sides lead to the same result for the sleeper but differ about ownerless objects.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps (introduces the second side of a question)
In general, in other cases
Ownerless objects
שבת residence; the spot from which one's 2000 אמות are measured

steps.whyThisMatters: The practical difference between the two sides is ownerless objects. Any source about how ownerless things move on שבת or יום טוב can now help decide the question.

phrases.english: Or perhaps,

phrases.aramaic: קָסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי בְּעָלְמָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri holds in general:
ownerless objects do not acquire residence,
and here this is the reason:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְנֵיעוֹר קָנָה, יָשֵׁן נָמֵי קָנָה?
phrases.english: since an awake person acquires, a sleeping one also acquires?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִילְמָא, קָסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי בְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the opposite reason for the same ruling, completing רבא's two-sided question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds that ownerless objects do not acquire שביתה, and bases the sleeper's ruling only on the awake/asleep logic.

steps.title: רב יוסף brings the case of rain that fell before יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף quotes a ברייתא. Rain that fell on ערב יום טוב gets 2000 אמות in every direction from where it fell. Rain that fell on יום טוב itself is like the feet of every person: it goes wherever the one who takes it may go.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Come and hear. Rain that fell before יום טוב has 2000 אמות in every direction. Rain that fell on יום טוב is like the feet of every person.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a source to try to answer רבא's question. This step only quotes the ברייתא; the next step shows how it helps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rain belongs to no one, so it is a perfect example of חפצי הפקר. The ברייתא says rain that was already there when יום טוב began 'settled' in its spot and got its own 2000 אמות. That sounds like ownerless objects acquiring שביתה, which is the first side of the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a source to settle a question)
Rain, rainwater
The day before יום טוב
2000 אמות in every direction
Like the feet of every person; it may go wherever its carrier may go

steps.confusionAlert: Rain that fell ON יום טוב is not forbidden to move. It has no spot of its own, so it simply follows whoever picks it up. Only rain that was there before יום טוב is tied to its own 2000 אמות.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Come and hear:
Rain that fell from the eve of the festival
phrases.notes: It was already in place when יום טוב began.

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לָהֶן אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה לְכׇל רוּחַ.
phrases.english: has two thousand cubits in every direction.
If it fell on the festival itself
it is like the feet of every person.
phrases.notes: It did not acquire residence, so it goes with whoever takes it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an outside ברייתא to try to decide between the two sides of רבא's question.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's question: do חפצי הפקר acquire שביתה according to רבי יוחנן בן נורי?
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about rain that fell before יום טוב versus on יום טוב.

steps.title: The rain ברייתא fits if ownerless objects acquire residence
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף begins his argument. If רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds that חפצי הפקר acquire שביתה, we can say whose view the rain ברייתא is: it follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say that רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds that ownerless objects acquire residence. Then whose view is this ברייתא? It is רבי יוחנן בן נורי's.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first half of a 'granted' argument. רב יוסף shows the ברייתא has an author under the first side. He is setting up the next move, which will ask who could have said it under the second side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rain is ownerless, yet it acquired its own 2000 אמות. So the ברייתא needs an author who holds that ownerless objects acquire שביתה. If רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds that view, he is a ready author. The implied problem, still to come, is that under the second side nobody holds this view.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out fine if you say (opens a 'granted' argument)
Whose view is this?

phrases.english: Granted, if you say
that Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri holds:
"ownerless objects acquire residence,"
then whose view is this? It is Rabbi Yochanan's.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא קָסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rain ברייתא to the first side of רבא's question, showing it has a clear author there.
steps.raayaObject: The first side: רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds חפצי הפקר קונין שביתה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rain ברייתא, which needs an author who holds that ownerless objects acquire residence.

steps.title: Without the ownerless view, the rain ברייתא fits no one
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף finishes his proof. If רבי יוחנן בן נורי held that חפצי הפקר do not acquire שביתה, the rain ברייתא would match neither רבי יוחנן בן נורי nor the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say that ownerless objects do not acquire a resting place, then whose view is this ברייתא? It is neither רבי יוחנן's nor the רבנן's!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף completes his argument by showing the other option leads to a dead end. The rain ברייתא would have no author.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rain ברייתא says rain that fell on ערב יום טוב gets 2000 אמות from where it landed. That means ownerless rain acquired שביתה. The רבנן clearly hold ownerless things do not acquire, so if רבי יוחנן בן נורי also held that, nobody would be left to author the ברייתא. So רבי יוחנן בן נורי must hold that חפצי הפקר acquire שביתה.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this? (asking which תנא authored a source)
Do not acquire a שבת/יום טוב resting place
The Sages, who disagree with רבי יוחנן בן נורי

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף's conclusion: רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds that חפצי הפקר acquire שביתה, and the rain ברייתא follows his view.

phrases.english: But if you say:
"Ownerless objects do not acquire a resting place,"
phrases.notes: This is the second option רבא raised in Step 6.

phrases.english: then whose view is this (rain ברייתא)?
Neither רבי יוחנן (בן נורי) nor the רבנן!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ חֶפְצֵי הֶפְקֵר אֵין קוֹנִין שְׁבִיתָה הָא מַנִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided argument begun in Step 8 by ruling out the other option.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds חפצי הפקר acquire שביתה (answering רבא's question).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about rain falling on ערב יום טוב getting 2000 אמות from its spot.

steps.title: Maybe the rain counts because the townspeople had it in mind
steps.stepSummary: While אביי repeats רב יוסף's teaching, רב ספרא suggests another reason the rain gets 2000 אמות: it fell near a city, and the townspeople intended to acquire it. If so, the rain was not acting as an ownerless object at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי was sitting and saying this teaching. רב ספרא said to אביי: Maybe we are dealing with rain near the city, and the people of that city had their minds on it!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא pushes back on the proof from the rain ברייתא. He gives another reason the rain might get 2000 אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's proof depended on the rain being truly ownerless. רב ספרא says the ברייתא might be about rain near a city that the residents planned to use. Then their intent, not the rain's ownerless status, gives it a place, and the proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or tradition (here, רב יוסף's argument)
But perhaps; introduces another possible reading
Near the city
Their minds were on it (they intended to acquire/use it)

phrases.aramaic: יְתֵיב אַבָּיֵי וְקָאָמַר לַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא.
phrases.english: אביי sat and was reciting this teaching.
phrases.notes: Scene-setting line that introduces רב ספרא's challenge.

phrases.english: רב ספרא said to אביי:
But perhaps we are dealing with rain near the city,
and the people of that city had their minds on it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא בִּגְשָׁמִים הַסְּמוּכִין לָעִיר עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof completed in Step 9 by reinterpreting the case in the rain ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the rain ברייתא, not רבי יוחנן בן נורי's view itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the rain was truly ownerless. It may have gained its place from the townspeople's intent.

steps.title: A city's cistern follows the city, not 2000 אמות from the cistern
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רב ספרא's challenge by turning to a different source. He quotes a משנה about cisterns. An individual's cistern follows the individual, and a city's cistern follows the city. The public cistern of עולי בבל, which has no owner, follows whoever draws from it. In the next step he sets this משנה against a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Don't think that! For we learned in a משנה: An individual's cistern is like the feet of that individual. The cistern of a city is like the feet of that city's people. And the cistern of the עולי בבל is like the feet of the one who draws the water.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins his answer to רב ספרא by quoting a משנה about cisterns. He is setting up a contradiction with a ברייתא in the next step, and that contradiction will show that some תנא holds ownerless objects acquire שביתה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line that matters for אביי is the last one. Ownerless public water (the עולי בבל cistern) has no שביתה of its own and simply follows whoever draws it. That fits the view that חפצי הפקר do not acquire שביתה. In the next step אביי contrasts it with a ברייתא that does give ownerless water its own place. This will show that some תנא holds that ownerless objects acquire.

keyTerms.meaning: It should not enter your mind; that idea is impossible
As we learned (in a משנה)
Cistern or water pit
Like the feet of; the item may go wherever that person may go
Those who came up from Babylonia; a public cistern belonging to everyone
The one who draws (fills from) the water

steps.confusionAlert: אביי does not argue from the wording of the rain ברייתא. He sets it aside and proves the point from a different pair of sources (this משנה and the ברייתא in the next step). That is why רב יוסף later asks why he did not answer 'from the ברייתא itself.'

phrases.english: He (אביי) said to him: It should not enter your mind,

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: בּוֹר שֶׁל יָחִיד — כְּרַגְלֵי יָחִיד,
phrases.english: as we learned: An individual's cistern is like the feet of that individual,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁל אוֹתָהּ הָעִיר — כְּרַגְלֵי אוֹתָהּ הָעִיר,
phrases.english: and that of a particular city is like the feet of that city's people,
phrases.notes: Part of the quoted משנה. רב יוסף will later use this kind of wording ('like the feet of that city') for his own, more direct rebuttal.

phrases.english: and that of the pilgrims from Babylonia is like the feet of the one who draws.
phrases.notes: This is אביי's key line. Ownerless public water acquires no place of its own here, which will be set against the שבטים ברייתא in the next step.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב ספרא's challenge from Step 10 and defends רב יוסף's proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejection of the alternate reading using a parallel source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ספרא: the rain gets 2000 אמות because the townspeople intended it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Through the contradiction between this משנה and the שבטים ברייתא, אביי shows that a תנא (רבי יוחנן בן נורי) holds ownerless objects acquire שביתה. So רב יוסף's understanding stands even without relying on the rain ברייתא.

steps.title: The משנה and a ברייתא about public cisterns contradict
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings a ברייתא: the cistern of the שבטים (ownerless, belonging to a whole tribe) gets 2000 אמות in every direction. This clashes with the משנה, where the עולי בבל public cistern is only like the feet of the one who draws. The two sources contradict.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught in a ברייתא: A cistern of the tribes has 2000 אמות in every direction. These sources contradict each other!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי sets two sources against each other about ownerless public water. This sets up the next move, which will explain how they relate to the dispute about חפצי הפקר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats ownerless public water as having no place of its own, since it follows the one who draws. That fits 'ownerless objects do not acquire.' The ברייתא gives ownerless tribal water its own 2000 אמות, which fits 'ownerless objects do acquire.' This is the same split as רבי יוחנן בן נורי versus the רבנן, which is why אביי raises it.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was taught (in a ברייתא)
The tribes; a cistern belonging to a whole tribe, with no single owner
In every direction
They contradict each other

steps.whyThisMatters: This contradiction is the heart of אביי's answer to רב ספרא. Resolving it in the next step shows that a real תנא holds that ownerless objects acquire שביתה, without relying on the rain ברייתא.

phrases.english: And it was taught: A cistern belonging to the tribes

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לָהֶן אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה לְכׇל רוּחַ.
phrases.english: has 2000 אמות in every direction.
They contradict each other!

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָין אַהֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's argument by setting the עולי בבל line of the משנה from Step 11 against a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of the משנה (עולי בבל cistern) with the ברייתא (cistern of the שבטים).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both cisterns are ownerless public water. The משנה gives the water no place of its own, while the ברייתא gives it 2000 אמות from its location.

steps.title: The two cistern sources follow two different opinions
steps.stepSummary: The contradiction between the משנה (cistern is like the feet of whoever draws) and the ברייתא (tribal cistern gets 2000 אמות) is resolved. The ברייתא follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי, and the משנה follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, must we not learn from this: this source follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי, and that source follows the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction from Step 12 by saying each source follows a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives the tribal cistern 2000 אמות from where it is. That only makes sense if an ownerless object acquires its own שביתה, which is רבי יוחנן בן נורי's view. The משנה says the water simply follows whoever draws it, which fits the רבנן, who hold ownerless objects acquire no שביתה. This is the goal of אביי's whole argument: it proves that רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds חפצי הפקר קונין שביתה, answering רבא's question without depending on the rain ברייתא that רב ספרא challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not so that… (introduces the forced conclusion)
Learn from it; we can conclude
This one… that one… (assigns two sources to two opinions)
The Sages, the majority opinion arguing with רבי יוחנן בן נורי

steps.whatToRemember: The tribal-cistern ברייתא follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי (ownerless objects acquire שביתה). The cistern משנה follows the רבנן (they do not). This backs up רב יוסף's claim about רבי יוחנן בן נורי.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not so — learn from it:
phrases.notes: Signals the only remaining way out of the contradiction.

phrases.english: this one is Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא of the cistern of the שבטים (2000 אמות).

phrases.english: that one is the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: The משנה: the cistern is like the feet of whoever draws.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: הָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי, הָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Step 12 and thereby supports רב יוסף's proof from Steps 8-9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the sources between two תנאים (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and ברייתא seem to give opposite rules for the same kind of ownerless public water.
steps.terutzMaskana: They follow the same מחלוקת as רבי יוחנן בן נורי and the רבנן, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: אביי reports his exchange with רב ספרא to רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: אביי comes before רב יוסף and tells him what רב ספרא objected and how אביי answered.
steps.simpleTranslation: When אביי came before רב יוסף, he said to him: This is what רב ספרא said, and this is how I answered him.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short story line that sets up the next move. אביי reports the debate to his teacher so that רב יוסף can respond.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is argued yet. The line recalls רב ספרא's objection from Step 10 (the rain fell near a city) and אביי's long answer from Steps 11-13 (the cistern משנה contradicts the tribal-cistern ברייתא, so a תנא holds that ownerless objects acquire). It prepares the stage for רב יוסף to offer a simpler answer from the rain ברייתא itself.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came before (his teacher)
I answered him back

phrases.english: When he (Abaye) came before Rav Yosef,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי קָאָמַר רַב סָפְרָא,
phrases.english: he said to him: This is what Rav Safra said,
and this is how I answered him.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי קָאָמַר רַב סָפְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Frames the whole רב ספרא / אביי exchange (Steps 10-13) as being reported back to רב יוסף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. This is a narrative transition introducing רב יוסף's response.

steps.title: רב יוסף: refute רב ספרא from the ברייתא itself
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks why אביי needed an outside משנה. If the rain fell near a city and the townspeople acquired it, how could the ברייתא say it gets 2000 אמות in every direction?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Why didn't you answer him from the ברייתא itself? If you think we are dealing with rain near a city, how can it say 'it has 2000 אמות in every direction'?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף offers a simpler way to reject רב ספרא's suggestion. He points to the wording of the rain ברייתא itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ספרא claimed the rain got its limits because nearby townspeople intended to acquire it. רב יוסף notes that the ברייתא measures 2000 אמות from where the rain is, in every direction. That is the language of an object with its own שביתה, not of something owned by a city. So the wording of the ברייתא already rules out רב ספרא's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: From the source itself
If it would enter your mind (if you were to think)
We are dealing with
In every direction

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְאַמַּאי לָא תֵּימָא לֵיהּ מִגּוּפַהּ?
phrases.english: He said to him: And why didn't you answer him from the source itself?
phrases.notes: That is, from the rain ברייתא, without bringing a separate משנה.

phrases.english: If it would enter your mind
that we are dealing with rain near a city —
phrases.notes: This is רב ספרא's suggestion from Step 10.

phrases.aramaic: הַאי ״יֵשׁ לָהֶן אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה לְכׇל רוּחַ״?!
phrases.english: then this 'they have two thousand cubits in every direction'?!
phrases.notes: Rhetorical: that wording would not fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי לָא תֵּימָא לֵיהּ מִגּוּפַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, more direct rejection of רב ספרא, in place of אביי's proof from the משנה in Step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב ספרא's reading that the rain was acquired by townspeople.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא's own measurement (2000 אמות in every direction from the rain) does not fit city-owned water.

steps.title: Town-owned rain would follow the townspeople's limits
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף finishes his point. If the townspeople had acquired the rain, the ברייתא should have said it is 'like the feet of the people of that city.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It should have needed to say: 'like the feet of the people of that city'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף completes his argument by stating what the ברייתא would have said if רב ספרא were right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water owned by a city takes on the city's limits, just as the משנה in Step 11 said. Since the ברייתא instead gives the rain its own 2000 אמות, the rain must be ownerless and acquiring שביתה by itself. That fits only רבי יוחנן בן נורי, so רב יוסף's original proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the feet of (follows the same תחום as)
It should have said; it was needed

steps.whatToRemember: The wording of the rain ברייתא itself proves the rain is ownerless with its own שביתה. רב ספרא's 'near the city' suggestion fails, and the ברייתא follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.confusionAlert: 'מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ' here does not mean 'he asked a question.' It means 'the text should have said'—it describes the wording we would expect if רב ספרא were right.

phrases.english: Why, 'like the feet of the people of that city'
phrases.notes: The wording expected for town-owned water.

phrases.english: it should have said!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא כְּרַגְלֵי אַנְשֵׁי אוֹתָהּ הָעִיר מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב יוסף's refutation begun in Step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The rain in the ברייתא acquires its own שביתה as an ownerless object. So the ברייתא follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי, confirming רב יוסף.

steps.title: Quoting the rain ברייתא: rain that falls on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the rain ברייתא and quotes its second clause: rain that falls on יום טוב is like the feet of all people.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: On יום טוב, it is like the feet of every person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the ברייתא in order to examine it. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the ברייתא said rain that fell before יום טוב gets 2000 אמות from where it fell. This second part says rain that falls on יום טוב itself has no fixed spot. Whoever draws it may carry it wherever he may walk. The גמרא is about to ask why this should be so.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said (quoting an earlier source for analysis)
Festival day
Like the feet of every person (may go wherever its drawer may go)

phrases.english: The Master said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּיוֹם טוֹב — הֲרֵי הֵן כְּרַגְלֵי כׇּל אָדָם.
phrases.english: On the Festival — it is like the feet of every person.
phrases.notes: Rain that fell on יום טוב itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: בְּיוֹם טוֹב הֲרֵי הֵן כְּרַגְלֵי כׇּל אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רב ספרא discussion and opens a new examination of the rain ברייתא itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain that falls on יום טוב follows the feet of whoever draws it.

steps.title: Shouldn't the rain have acquired שביתה in the ocean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the clause. The water was in the ocean when יום טוב began, so it should have acquired שביתה there and now be out of its limits.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why? Let it acquire שביתה in the ocean!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's rule about rain that falls on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rain comes from ocean water that rises into clouds. At the start of יום טוב this water was in the ocean, so by the logic that ownerless things acquire שביתה, its home spot should be there. It then traveled far beyond 2000 אמות, so it should be forbidden to carry it at all, not 'like the feet of every person.'

keyTerms.meaning: And why? (introduces a challenge)
Let it acquire a place of rest (שביתה)
The ocean

steps.confusionAlert: The question assumes rain comes from ocean water lifted into the clouds. The point is that the water already existed somewhere when יום טוב began. It is not 'new' water.

phrases.english: And why?
Let it acquire residence in the ocean.
phrases.notes: Where the water was at the onset of יום טוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי? לִיקְנֵי שְׁבִיתָה בְּאוֹקְיָינוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the clause quoted in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that rain falling on יום טוב is like the feet of every person.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ownerless objects acquire שביתה, the water should have acquired it in the ocean at the start of יום טוב. It would then be outside its limits and forbidden to move.

steps.title: The question only works according to רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the rain ברייתא must not follow רבי אליעזר. This is because רבי אליעזר holds that all rain comes from ocean water.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say that the ברייתא does not follow רבי אליעזר. If it followed רבי אליעזר, there would be a problem, because he said: 'The whole world drinks from the waters of the ocean.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens the question from the last step. It says the ברייתא seems not to follow רבי אליעזר, because according to him the rain really did come from the ocean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem in Step 18 depends on one idea: that rainwater was sitting in the ocean when יום טוב began. That idea is רבי אליעזר's view, that ocean water rises and becomes rain. So the גמרא suggests the ברייתא follows the other view and not רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say. This introduces a suggestion the גמרא may later reject.
Not according to (a certain opinion)
The ocean
Drinks. Here it means the world gets its rain from that source.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a brand new topic. It finishes the question from Step 18 by showing which opinion that question depends on.

phrases.english: Let us say it is not according to Rabbi Eliezer,
because if it were according to Rabbi Eliezer —
he said: the entire world
drinks from the waters of the ocean!
phrases.notes: Meaning: rain comes from ocean water that rises into the clouds.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge from Step 18 by tying it to רבי אליעזר's view about where rain comes from.
steps.kashyaTarget: The second clause of the ברייתא: rain on יום טוב is like the feet of all people.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי אליעזר, the rain was ocean water when יום טוב began. So it should have a limit from the ocean. This suggests the ברייתא cannot follow him.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: the clouds formed before יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק explains that the ברייתא can follow even רבי אליעזר. It is talking about clouds that had already formed before יום טוב began.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: Here we are dealing with clouds that had already gathered on ערב יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers the question. He limits the ברייתא to a case where the clouds already existed before יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the clouds formed before יום טוב, then the water was already up in the clouds when יום טוב began, not in the ocean. So the water never got 'stuck' in the ocean and never left its limits on יום טוב. This way even רבי אליעזר can agree with the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Clouds
That were gathered or formed
The day before the festival
We are dealing with (a specific case)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Here, with clouds that had formed
from the eve of the festival, we are dealing.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּעָבִים שֶׁנִּתְקַשְּׁרוּ מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Steps 18-19 so that the ברייתא can fit רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the rainwater was in the ocean when יום טוב started, so it should be outside its limits.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא speaks of clouds that formed before יום טוב. The water was already in the clouds, so it never got a limit from the ocean.

steps.title: Maybe these are different clouds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: maybe the clouds from before יום טוב moved away, and the rain came from new clouds that did come from the ocean on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe those clouds went away, and these are other clouds?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יצחק's answer. How do we know the rain came from the same clouds that existed before יום טוב?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק's answer only works if the rain came from the old clouds. Clouds move all the time. The rain could have fallen from new clouds that formed on יום טוב from ocean water, and then the original problem comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps
Those (ones)
Went away
Others

phrases.english: But perhaps those clouds went away,
and these are other clouds?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא הָנָךְ אָזְלִי, וְהָנָךְ אַחֲרִינֵי נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יצחק's answer from Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's claim that the rain came from clouds formed before יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: We cannot be sure the rain fell from the same clouds. It may have come from new clouds made of ocean water on יום טוב.

steps.title: The clouds have an identifying sign
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case is one where the clouds have a sign, so we know they are the same clouds.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where they have an identifying sign on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 21. We are talking about clouds that can be recognized, so we know they are the same ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This narrows רבי יצחק's case even further. It applies only when there is clear proof that the clouds which dropped the rain are the same clouds from before יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: An identifying sign
In them (on them)

phrases.english: Where they have an identifying sign in them.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִית לְהוּ סִימָנָא בְּגַוַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the rain came from new clouds.
steps.terutzMaskana: The clouds have a recognizable sign, so we know they are the original clouds.

steps.title: Second answer: a doubt in a rabbinic law is treated leniently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives another answer. Even without a sign, the question of whether these are the same clouds is a doubt in a rabbinic law, and we may be lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: this is a doubt in a rabbinic law, and in a doubt in a rabbinic law we are lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second, separate answer to the question about new clouds. It uses the rule that when we are unsure about a rabbinic law, we may rule leniently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The limit being discussed here is a rabbinic law (דרבנן). So even if we cannot tell whether these are old or new clouds, we do not need to be strict. We follow the lenient side and treat the rain as the old clouds' water. This answer does not need a sign at all.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say. This introduces a second answer.
A doubt or uncertainty
Their words, meaning a rabbinic law (דרבנן)
To be lenient

steps.whatToRemember: The rain ברייתא can fit even רבי אליעזר. The rain comes from clouds formed before יום טוב. We know they are the same clouds either because they have a sign, or because a doubt in a rabbinic law is treated leniently (סָפֵק דְּרַבָּנָן לְקוּלָּא).
steps.whyThisMatters: סָפֵק דְּרַבָּנָן לְקוּלָּא is a basic rule used all over ש״ס: when we are unsure about a rabbinic law, we may be lenient.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
it is a doubt regarding a rabbinic law,
and a doubt regarding a rabbinic law is treated leniently.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָוֵי סָפֵק דְּדִבְרֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to Step 21, in place of the answer in Step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: General rule of doubt (סָפֵק דְּרַבָּנָן לְקוּלָּא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without a sign, we must worry that the rain came from new clouds made of ocean water.
steps.terutzMaskana: The doubt is about a rabbinic law, so we follow the lenient side and do not worry about new clouds.

steps.title: Why doesn't the water get a home in the clouds?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the rain water does not get its שביתה in the clouds, where it was when יום טוב started.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let the water acquire its resting place in the clouds!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's ruling that rain is 'like everyone's feet.' This question also sets up the proof that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוחנן בן נורי, whom this ברייתא follows, even an ownerless object gets a home base (שביתה) where it is when יום טוב begins, and its 2,000 אמה limit is measured from there. The rain water was sitting in the clouds at that moment. So why not say the clouds are its home, and its limit is measured from the clouds?

keyTerms.meaning: Let it acquire
Resting place, the home base an object gets when שבת or יום טוב begins
Clouds

phrases.english: But let it acquire residence in the clouds!
phrases.notes: 'It' means the rain water that later fell on יום טוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיקְנִי שְׁבִיתָה בְּעָבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the case of clouds that already formed before יום טוב, and asks why those clouds are not the water's home base.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that rain water is 'like the feet of every person.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The water was in the clouds when יום טוב began, so by normal rules it should get its שביתה there and be limited by that spot.

steps.title: Proof that there are no תחומין above ten טפחים
steps.stepSummary: Since the ברייתא does not give the water a home in the clouds, the גמרא wants to prove that תחומין do not apply above ten טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Solve from this that there are no תחומין above ten טפחים. For if there were תחומין up there, the water would acquire its resting place in the clouds!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the question it just asked to answer a different open question: do the rules of תחומין apply high up, above ten טפחים from the ground?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא clearly does not treat the clouds as the water's home. The גמרא suggests the reason is that high in the air there are no תחומין at all, so nothing can get a שביתה up there. If תחומין did apply up there, the water would surely get its home in the clouds.

keyTerms.meaning: Solve [the open question] from this
The שבת/יום טוב travel limits of 2,000 אמות
Higher than ten טפחים above the ground

steps.whyThisMatters: Whether תחומין apply above ten טפחים is a famous open question (for example, someone walking on poles or flying in the air). The גמרא is testing whether this ברייתא can settle it.

phrases.english: Resolve from this
phrases.notes: Used when the גמרא thinks a source can settle an open question.

phrases.english: that there are no Shabbat limits above ten handbreadths.
For if there were Shabbat limits [up there],
let it acquire residence in the clouds!
phrases.notes: The same words as the previous step, now used as the logic of the proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּיפְשׁוֹט מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the question of step 24 into a proof about the open question of תחומין above ten טפחים.
steps.raayaObject: That there are no תחומין above ten טפחים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that treats rain as 'like everyone's feet' and does not give it a שביתה in the clouds.

steps.title: Rejection: water inside clouds is absorbed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: there may be תחומין above ten טפחים, but water inside a cloud is absorbed and cannot get a שביתה there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, I can tell you: there are תחומין above ten טפחים. But the water in the cloud is absorbed inside it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from the previous step. It gives a different reason why the water does not get its home in the clouds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed the only reason for no שביתה in the clouds was that there are no תחומין up there. The גמרא offers another reason: inside the cloud the water is absorbed and is not in its normal form, so it is not a distinct object that can get a home. So the ברייתא proves nothing about תחומין above ten טפחים, and that question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, I can tell you (a phrase that opens a rejection)
Water
Cloud
They are absorbed (swallowed up) inside

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about rain does not prove there are no תחומין above ten טפחים. Water absorbed in a cloud cannot get a שביתה, so the open question stays unsolved.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does NOT decide that there ARE תחומין above ten טפחים. It only says 'I could say there are,' to show that the proof fails.

phrases.english: Actually, I can say to you:
there are Shabbat limits [above ten],
but the water in the cloud is absorbed.
phrases.notes: Absorbed water is not in its usual form, so it does not acquire a resting place.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 25 and answers the question of step 24 in another way.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof that there are no תחומין above ten טפחים. It does not reject the ברייתא's ruling about rain.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof wrongly assumed that 'no תחומין up there' is the only possible reason the water gets no שביתה in the clouds. Absorption is another reason.
